findings.issue_text: [High/concurrency] flusher.py `_ensure_processes_alive`: in thread mode (produce_to_pipe set), `process.kill()` is skipped for non-multiprocessing.Process and `_create_process_for_shards` immediately replaces the process entry, so the hung thread keeps flushing the same shards, causing duplicate Kafka production and concurrent Redis access alongside the replacement thread

[Medium/bug] flusher.py:52 — `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats flusher_processes=0 as 'use all shards'; a negative value yields num_processes < 0, an empty processes map, and no flusher with data accumulating in Redis and no error; should validate flusher_processes >= 1

[Medium/bug] flusher.py `join` — if deadline expires while waiting on the first process, `break` exits the loop entirely, leaving remaining processes never waited on or terminated so they can linger and flush after shutdown; old code terminated the single process unconditionally

[Medium/data] flusher.py (~line 180) — metrics.timing('spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes', tags={'shard': shard_tag}) mislabels the metric since one process handles multiple shards, aggregating several shards under a comma-joined 'shard' tag; tag should be dropped or per-shard breakdown added

[Low/data] flusher.py (~line 190) — inconsistent metric tag naming: 'spans.buffer.flusher.produce' uses "shard" while 'spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce' uses "shards", breaking dashboards/alerts keyed on tag name

[Low/doc_defect] flusher.py:31-32 — docstring says 'one process per shard' but implementation shares shards across processes via i % num_processes; also unused `_create_process_for_shard` reflects the same incorrect model
[Low/bug] flusher.py `_create_process_for_shard` — dead code, never called, and its `shard in shards` membership scan silently does nothing if the shard isn't found; should be removed or wired in

[Medium/test_gap] test_flusher.py / test_consumer.py — no test covers the restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive` with a dead/hung process and multiple processes), despite materially changed restart semantics (per-process restart counters, buffer recreation)

[Low/bug] test_consumer.py:12 — changing test_basic from django_db to django_db(transaction=True) weakens isolation for the whole suite to accommodate the extra flusher poll/sleep; the added time.sleep(0.1) also introduces a timing-dependent assertion

[Low/api] consumers/__init__.py:434 — --flusher-processes option is added unconditionally to ingest_transactions_options but only takes effect in ProcessSpansStrategyFactory; passing it to other consumers sharing this option set would raise an unexpected-kwarg TypeError; verify the option set isn't shared

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/concurrency] flusher.py `_ensure_processes_alive`: in thread mode (produce_to_pipe set), `process.kill()` is skipped for non-multiprocessing.Process and `_create_process_for_shards` immediately replaces the process entry, so the hung thread keeps flushing the same shards, causing duplicate Kafka production and concurrent Redis access alongside the replacement thread

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, when `produce_to_pipe` is set the flusher uses `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`) and stores it in `self.processes[process_index]`. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on unhealthy/hung detection it only attempts `process.kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so a hung thread is not stopped. It then immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, starting a new thread for the same shard set and overwriting the entry in `self.processes`, leaving the old (still-alive) thread running. That can lead to concurrent flushing/Redis access for the same shards and duplicate Kafka production in thread mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] flusher.py:52 — `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats flusher_processes=0 as 'use all shards'; a negative value yields num_processes < 0, an empty processes map, and no flusher with data accumulating in Redis and no error; should validate flusher_processes >= 1

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will treat an explicitly provided `max_processes=0` as falsy and silently fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, which is likely unintended for a CLI/option value. Also, a negative `max_processes` propagates into `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))`, making `range(self.num_processes)` empty and then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` yields an index not present in `process_to_shards_map`, causing a runtime failure during shard assignment. The diff shows no validation that `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` is >= 1.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that breaking out of the loop when the deadline expires stops processing the remaining flusher processes, so they are neither waited on nor terminated and may continue running after shutdown—same core issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] flusher.py (~line 180) — metrics.timing('spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes', tags={'shard': shard_tag}) mislabels the metric since one process handles multiple shards, aggregating several shards under a comma-joined 'shard' tag; tag should be dropped or per-shard breakdown added

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, `shard_tag` is built as a comma-joined list of shards handled by that process (`shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))`), and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` (and related timers) will therefore emit a `shard` tag value that can represent multiple shards, not a single shard. Given the diff explicitly introduces multi-shard-per-process mapping (`process_to_shards_map`) this finding is grounded: the tag semantics are now ambiguous/misleading unless the metric is intended to be “shards”/group-level rather than per-shard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] flusher.py:31-32 — docstring says 'one process per shard' but implementation shares shards across processes via i % num_processes; also unused `_create_process_for_shard` reflects the same incorrect model

adjudication.rationale: The updated class docstring says “Creates one process per shard”, but the implementation can intentionally share multiple shards per process when `max_processes` is set: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and shards are distributed via `process_index = i % self.num_processes` into `process_to_shards_map`. This is a documentation/clarity mismatch rather than a functional defect. Also, `_create_process_for_shard` is added but not referenced anywhere in the diff, making it dead code that reinforces the incorrect per-shard mental model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] flusher.py `_create_process_for_shard` — dead code, never called, and its `shard in shards` membership scan silently does nothing if the shard isn't found; should be removed or wired in

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` in `flusher.py`, but no code in the shown changes calls it (the lifecycle uses `_create_processes()`, `_create_process_for_shards()`, and `_ensure_processes_alive()`), so it is effectively dead/unused within this PR. Additionally, its loop will simply fall through if the shard is not present in `process_to_shards_map` (no log/exception), which could hide mistakes if it were ever used. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability issue rather than a currently verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] test_flusher.py / test_consumer.py — no test covers the restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive` with a dead/hung process and multiple processes), despite materially changed restart semantics (per-process restart counters, buffer recreation)

adjudication.rationale: Diff materially changes restart/health semantics in `SpanFlusher`: single `self.process`/`self.healthy_since`/`self.backpressure_since` is replaced with per-process maps and `_ensure_processes_alive()` now loops processes, tracks `process_restarts[process_index]`, kills/recreates a specific process, and recreates per-process `SpansBuffer` (`_create_process_for_shards`, `self.buffers[...] = shard_buffer`). The updated/added tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and `test_flusher` backpressure assertion) verify basic flow, process-count limiting, and backpressure presence, but none exercises the new restart paths (dead process via `is_alive()==False` or hang via `process_healthy_since` exceeding `max-unhealthy-seconds`) nor asserts correct per-process restart counter behavior/buffer recreation. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing coverage for new nontrivial logic, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] test_consumer.py:12 — changing test_basic from django_db to django_db(transaction=True) weakens isolation for the whole suite to accommodate the extra flusher poll/sleep; the added time.sleep(0.1) also introduces a timing-dependent assertion

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes only `test_basic` (and a new test) to `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)`, which applies per-test, not “for the whole suite,” so the claim about weakening isolation across the entire suite isn’t supported by the diff. Also, the added `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is not timing-dependent here because the test immediately monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so that sleep becomes a no-op (and there’s no new timing-based assertion introduced).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] consumers/__init__.py:434 — --flusher-processes option is added unconditionally to ingest_transactions_options but only takes effect in ProcessSpansStrategyFactory; passing it to other consumers sharing this option set would raise an unexpected-kwarg TypeError; verify the option set isn't shared

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new `--flusher-processes` click option is added only within the specific consumer config entry for `"process-spans"` in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py` (it’s appended to that entry’s `click_options` list). It is not added “unconditionally to ingest_transactions_options” nor shown being shared by other consumers’ option sets in this diff, so the claimed unexpected-kwarg risk for other consumers isn’t verifiable from the changes shown.
